01 / Lead study

From a concept model
to a guided visit.

Dubai Residence is an independent, AI-assisted visualization study. Its Blender-built model becomes a browser-based experience with places to look, rooms to enter, and a clear route through the home.

Visual exploration / kitchen + dining

From model frame
to material mood.

An unaltered Blender render anchors the composition. A separate AI-assisted study explores a warmer material and lighting direction for the same kitchen and dining view.

What changes: the generated image adds illustrative finishes, planting, lighting, and furniture details. Those generated details are not in the interactive 3D tour, were not measured or client-approved, and this visual was not commissioned.

What the study demonstrates

One story across stills, model, and movement.

The viewer brings together a guided first-person route, room anchors, a two-floor navigation schematic, and a short residence film. These are presentation tools for reviewing a concept with collaborators or prospective buyers.

02 / Interactive presentation

03 / Review context
Navigation, a viewing sequence, and documented visual and browser checks.

Study boundary. This is a fictional, unbuilt residence. Its plan is a navigation schematic, not a measured architectural drawing. The study is not BIM, engineering, construction documentation, or proof of property sales. The public 3D viewer and film played in a browser check on 28 September 2026; other linked projects were not rechecked live.

For a defined property brief

A presentation package
with a clear handoff.

A possible engagement can begin with one space or a single presentation sequence. The exact scope depends on the source material, review audience, and agreed acceptance criteria.

What to include in a brief ↗
  1. 01

    Establish the story

    Agree on the space, intended audience, references, and what a viewer needs to understand.

  2. 02

    Build the visual route

    Develop the selected views, model or walkthrough, and a sequence for feedback.

  3. 03

    Deliver reviewable evidence

    Share agreed files and browser checks with known limits and a focused revision pass.

02 / Interface & campaign

Design with the
next step in view.

Two separate Figma studies show how an interface explains an action and how one visual language adapts across campaign formats. Both are self-initiated demonstrations.

UI concept / Figma / fictional service

ПУТЬ — parcel experience

Two editable desktop screens connect shipment status to pickup action. The case documents Button variants, empty and not-found states, and a separately labeled mobile proposal.

Full design case ↗Figma source ↗

Self-initiated demo with fictional service and data. Image shown is a Figma export. The mobile layouts are local proposals, not Figma frames or validated product screens. No client outcome is claimed.

Campaign concept / Figma / fictional brand

ТИШЕ — one idea, three formats

A coordinated post, vertical story, and web banner keep the offer and visual hierarchy recognizable as their compositions change.

Figma file ↗Case record ↗

Self-initiated demo; brand and product are fictional. Image shown was rendered locally from SVG, not exported from Figma. The campaign was not launched.

03 / Game prototypes

Worlds that can be
tested, not just pictured.

Independent prototypes with source files, screenshots, and documented checks. These show implementation range; they are not commissioned game releases.

Roblox Studio / Luau / playable local demos

Courses, rounds & progression

AeroRun, Lava Rush, and Floor Is Lava + Economy demonstrate checkpoint flow, round rules, responsive HUDs, and a saved player profile in a separate Studio test.

AI-assisted portfolio demos. The source repository is private; this screenshot is from a local Studio demo. A public player launch, independent playtests, and client adoption are not claimed.

Awakening
